item.title: Cyanotype postcards
item.description:
A Christmas postcard doesn’t have to be made with ink: it can be made with the sun. In this afternoon we coat paper with cyanotype, lay objects and negatives on it and let the light do the rest. Each student takes theirs home, made and developed on the spot.

It’s Friday 11 December, at the Nau Bostik.

What we’ll do

  1. The mix. We prepare the cyanotype solution and coat the paper.
  2. The composition. Postcards with objects, plants, cut-outs and negatives (photocopies on transparent paper).
  3. The exposure. In December the sun is low and the prints need more minutes; we use that to understand why.
  4. The development. Water and that’s it. We watch the blue appear.

What’s included

All the materials: paper, cyanotype solution, objects, trays and water. Each student takes a set of postcards home.

item.title: Spirit photography
item.description:
In the late 19th century, there were photographers who claimed to photograph spirits. In reality they used two things we master: exposure time and double exposure. In this workshop we teach you how they did it and put it into practice for Castanyada.

It will be on Saturday 31 October, from 7 to 10 pm, at Nau Bostik.

What we’ll do

  1. The history. 19th-century spirit photography and the fraud of the spiritualist photographers, with real examples.
  2. The technique. Long exposures with figures that move or vanish mid-exposure, and double exposures in camera.
  3. The practice. A session at Nau Bostik in low light, with torches, sheets and costumes to make our own apparitions.
  4. The developing. You can develop the film with us in a later session, if you like.

What’s included

One black-and-white film per student. If you have a camera with Bulb mode or multiple exposure, bring it; if not, we can lend you one.

item.title: Analogue portrait
item.description:
The person in front of the camera

Photographing a person is different from photographing anything else. It’s not just the light, not just the technique. It’s the relationship. The way you approach, how you talk, how you make someone feel at ease in front of a lens. Without that, the best light in the world means nothing.

In this workshop we work in the Llumàtics studio: paper backgrounds, quality flash units and analogue camera. Each student takes turns as photographer and subject, and at the end we review the frames together.
